packet.headline_seed: Vibe coding platform Base44 launches own model as AI startups seek defensibility
packet.description_seed: Wix-owned vibe coding platform Base44 has started rolling out its own AI model — with hopes that it will eventually outperform frontier models.

what: Vibe coding platform Base44 launches own model as AI startups seek defensibility

clean_source_blocks.text: Wix-owned vibe coding platform Base44 has started rolling out its own AI model — with hopes that it will eventually outperform frontier models.

Base44, the vibe coding platform that Wix acquired for $80 million just one year ago — when the company was barely six moths old and had a team of eight — has started rolling out its own AI model to support its users in creating apps with natural language. The move comes as the discussion in AI circles has intensified over whether frontier models are best suited for all use cases. A related question is whether businesses built on top of someone else’s models are truly defensible long-term. The latest move of Base44, based in the Bay Area, speaks to both. ---

NEW YORK – Base44, the AI-powered platform that enables anyone to create production-ready applications using natural language, today announced the launch of its first proprietary AI model, now in production and actively serving users on the platform. The milestone marks a defining moment in Base44's evolution, from an AI-powered platform to a full-stack AI company with deep, end-to-end capabilities spanning data, infrastructure, training, and deployment.The custom LLM was developed and optimized using Base44's vast and unique dataset generated from tens of millions of real user interactions on the platform. The result is a model already demonstrating competitive performance against the foundation models it replaces, with an opportunity to surpass them as training continues on Base44's unique and growing dataset."As the first app-creation platform to launch its own proprietary AI model, this is a big step for us as a company," said Maor Shlomo, Founder and CEO of Base44. "Having our own model means we can continue to improve it over time, making us less dependent on external vendors. This is not a trivial effort. It requires deep expertise, significant infrastructure, and access to the kind of rich, diverse data that most organizations simply do not have."The new model represents a very ambitious custom model development effort underway in the industry. Unlike most companies that train models for narrow, single-purpose use cases, Base44 has built a general-purpose AI agent capable of handling both conversation and coding tasks, including complex multi-turn interactions, tool usage, runtime management, and backend operations.Base44's ability to build and deploy its own model is the result of deliberate investment across several key areas:

That deal is just the latest in a broader wave of acquisitions and partnerships sweeping through the vibe-coding space. In July, AI startup Cognition snatched up Windsurf after OpenAI's $3 billion deal to acquire the vibe coding tool maker fell through. Just one month earlier, web design platform Wix bought Base44, a six-month-old startup bootstrapped by a solo founder, for $80 million. These entrants are competing with far bigger and better-funded players, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Microsoft, that make their own AI-powered coding tools. Yet, the rise of these tools is also rattling the broader market: Some tech giants saw their shares take a hit as investors dumped legacy software stocks over concerns that AI and vibe coding will allow companies to build their own software rather than buy.

payload.title: Base44 ottaa käyttöön oman tekoälymallinsa sovellusten rakentamiseen
payload.summary: Wixin omistama Base44 on alkanut ottaa käyttöön omaa tekoälymalliaan, jolla käyttäjät voivat rakentaa sovelluksia luonnollisella kielellä. Yhtiön mukaan oma malli vähentää riippuvuutta ulkoisista mallitoimittajista.
payload.content:
Wixin omistama Base44 on tuonut tuotantokäyttöön ensimmäisen oman tekoälymallinsa, jonka tarkoitus on tukea käyttäjiä sovellusten luomisessa luonnollisella kielellä. Julkistus osuu aikaan, jolloin tekoälyalalla arvioidaan yhä tarkemmin, riittävätkö suurten toimijoiden yleismallit kaikkiin käyttötapauksiin ja voivatko niiden päälle rakennetut yritykset puolustaa asemaansa pitkällä aikavälillä.

## Oma malli käyttöön käyttäjille

Base44 kuvaa itseään tekoälypohjaiseksi alustaksi, jonka avulla käyttäjät voivat luoda tuotantovalmiita sovelluksia luonnollisella kielellä. Yhtiön mukaan uusi oma kielimalli on jo tuotannossa ja palvelee aktiivisesti alustan käyttäjiä.

Mallia on kehitetty ja optimoitu Base44:n omalla aineistolla, jota on kertynyt kymmenistä miljoonista käyttäjävuorovaikutuksista alustalla. Yhtiö sanoo mallin osoittavan jo kilpailukykyistä suorituskykyä suhteessa niihin perustason malleihin, joita se korvaa, ja näkee mahdollisuuden parantaa sitä edelleen aineiston kasvaessa.

Base44:n perustaja ja toimitusjohtaja Maor Shlomo sanoi oman mallin olevan yhtiölle iso askel. Hänen mukaansa se antaa Base44:lle mahdollisuuden kehittää mallia ajan mittaan ja vähentää riippuvuutta ulkoisista toimittajista. Shlomo korosti myös, että tällainen työ vaatii syvää osaamista, merkittävää infrastruktuuria ja laajaa, monipuolista dataa.

## Vibe coding -markkina kiristyy

Base44:n taustalla on nopea kasvu ja yrityskauppa. Wix osti yhtiön noin 80 miljoonalla dollarilla, kun startup oli vasta noin puolen vuoden ikäinen ja sen tiimissä oli kahdeksan henkilöä. Base44 toimii Bay Arealla.

Yhtiön oma malli on rakennettu yleiskäyttöiseksi tekoälyagentiksi, jonka kerrotaan käsittelevän sekä keskustelua että koodaustehtäviä. Sen kuvataan tukevan myös monivaiheisia vuorovaikutuksia, työkalujen käyttöä, ajonaikaista hallintaa ja taustajärjestelmien toimintoja.

Kilpailu niin sanotussa vibe coding -kentässä on samalla kiihtynyt. Markkinoilla liikkuvat sekä startupit että suuret teknologiayhtiöt, kuten OpenAI, Anthropic ja Microsoft, joilla on omia tekoälypohjaisia koodaustyökaluja. Alan yrityskaupat ja kumppanuudet ovat lisääntyneet, ja sijoittajat ovat seuranneet tarkasti, voiko tekoälypohjainen sovelluskehitys vähentää perinteisten ohjelmistojen kysyntää.
summary_bullets: Base44 on ottanut tuotantokäyttöön ensimmäisen oman tekoälymallinsa.
Yhtiö sanoo mallin hyödyntävän kymmenistä miljoonista käyttäjävuorovaikutuksista kertynyttä aineistoa.
Oma malli voi vähentää riippuvuutta ulkoisista mallitoimittajista kiristyvässä tekoälykoodaamisen kilpailussa.

Wix-owned vibe coding platform Base44 has started rolling out its own AI model — with hopes that it will eventually outperform frontier models.

Base44, the vibe coding platform that Wix acquired for $80 million just one year ago — when the company was barely six moths old and had a team of eight — has started rolling out its own AI model to support its users in creating apps with natural language. The move comes as the discussion in AI circles has intensified over whether frontier models are best suited for all use cases. A related question is whether businesses built on top of someone else’s models are truly defensible long-term. The latest move of Base44, based in the Bay Area, speaks to both. ---

NEW YORK – Base44, the AI-powered platform that enables anyone to create production-ready applications using natural language, today announced the launch of its first proprietary AI model, now in production and actively serving users on the platform. The milestone marks a defining moment in Base44's evolution, from an AI-powered platform to a full-stack AI company with deep, end-to-end capabilities spanning data, infrastructure, training, and deployment.The custom LLM was developed and optimized using Base44's vast and unique dataset generated from tens of millions of real user interactions on the platform. The result is a model already demonstrating competitive performance against the foundation models it replaces, with an opportunity to surpass them as training continues on Base44's unique and growing dataset."As the first app-creation platform to launch its own proprietary AI model, this is a big step for us as a company," said Maor Shlomo, Founder and CEO of Base44. "Having our own model means we can continue to improve it over time, making us less dependent on external vendors. This is not a trivial effort. It requires deep expertise, significant infrastructure, and access to the kind of rich, diverse data that most organizations simply do not have."The new model represents a very ambitious custom model development effort underway in the industry. Unlike most companies that train models for narrow, single-purpose use cases, Base44 has built a general-purpose AI agent capable of handling both conversation and coding tasks, including complex multi-turn interactions, tool usage, runtime management, and backend operations.Base44's ability to build and deploy its own model is the result of deliberate investment across several key areas:

That deal is just the latest in a broader wave of acquisitions and partnerships sweeping through the vibe-coding space. In July, AI startup Cognition snatched up Windsurf after OpenAI's $3 billion deal to acquire the vibe coding tool maker fell through. Just one month earlier, web design platform Wix bought Base44, a six-month-old startup bootstrapped by a solo founder, for $80 million. These entrants are competing with far bigger and better-funded players, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Microsoft, that make their own AI-powered coding tools. Yet, the rise of these tools is also rattling the broader market: Some tech giants saw their shares take a hit as investors dumped legacy software stocks over concerns that AI and vibe coding will allow companies to build their own software rather than buy.
